metrics.label: Henry Hub gas

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam

brief.text:
The clearest news in today's data is another attack on a tanker near the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway at the mouth of the Arabian Gulf through which much of the world's crude moves. UKMTO reported on Friday that a tanker caught fire after being struck by a projectile while sailing outbound, extending a run of attacks. For anyone fixing ships (agreeing a charter), that keeps war-risk insurance, crew willingness and owner appetite for Gulf liftings in play. Set against that, Banchero Costa reports Arabian Gulf crude exports down 27.6% over January-October, meaning less cargo to carry out of the region.

On prices, Brent crude was $92.57 a barrel today, up $1.19 (+1.3%), and WTI $83.62, up $1.18 (+1.4%), with the Brent-WTI spread at $8.95. The data does not show why crude firmed; one trade-press headline says oil fell for a third straight week on Friday on strong Middle East exports despite Hormuz disruption, and another says the Iran war premium has evaporated amid surging supply, so this may simply be a partial bounce. Henry Hub US gas was $3.47/mmBtu, up 6.1%, unexplained in this data. Bunker fuel split: VLSFO (the main low-sulphur marine fuel) was $842/t in Singapore today, up $8, while Rotterdam fell $9.50 to $705.50, Fujairah $800 and Houston $720.50. No freight benchmark refreshed today: the Baltic Dry Index, which tracks dry bulk cargo rates, stood at 2,898 on Friday 20 November, down 3 points, with Capesize (the largest bulkers) at 4,502 and Panamax at 2,140. VLCC earnings on the Gulf-China route were last published at $1,078,714/day on Sunday 15 November — six days old, not today's market.

Running stories: Hormuz escalation developed with Friday's strike. The Los Angeles-Long Beach strike threat advanced — more than 110 US trade associations are urging a deal as the deadline nears. Shadow-fleet sanctions got a new angle: the Russian Navy is reported escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers in the Mediterranean. Russian refinery damage and diesel export limits, and the US-China ship fee suspension, had no news today and are unchanged. LNG spot shipping rates fell for a second week, per Spark Commodities.

Watch two things: whether LA-Long Beach talks settle before the deadline, since a stoppage hits container berths and inland flows; and MEPC 85 in London from 30 November, where IMO decarbonisation rules affecting fuel choice will be argued out.

storylines.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue. UKMTO said on Friday that another tanker was struck by a projectile and caught fire while outbound through the strait, extending a wave of attacks on merchant ships.
storylines.why_it_matters: Hull strikes raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings, slow transits and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude, product and gas ton-miles.
storylines.latest: A further tanker was hit and set on fire in the strait on Friday; separately, Banchero Costa reports Arabian Gulf crude exports down 27.6% in January-October.

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea have continued through November, with two vessels sunk off Bulgaria and crew injured following an earlier wheat carrier capsizing.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region.
storylines.latest: No direct update today; trade press notes the Russian Navy has lost ships in the Black Sea and is stretched by escort duties.
sources: Russian Navy Back in the Mediterranean Escorting a Cargo Flotilla

storylines.title: Russian refining damage and diesel export limits
storylines.what: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October, on top of a Russian ban on most diesel exports extended to end-January.
storylines.why_it_matters: Lost Russian refining and export restrictions reshape clean product ton-miles, pulling diesel from longer-haul sources and changing MR and LR employment.

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations. The Russian Navy is now reported escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers and a cargo flotilla in the Mediterranean.
storylines.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties and vessel positions, and naval escorting signals that sanctioned trades are being defended rather than curtailed.
storylines.latest: Reports that the Russian Navy, stretched after Black Sea losses, is escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers in the Mediterranean.
sources: Russian Navy Back in the Mediterranean Escorting a Cargo Flotilla

storylines.title: US-China ship fees and port state control friction
storylines.what: The US has extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue, while a US congressional committee urges sanctions over China's detention of Panama-flagged ships.
storylines.why_it_matters: Reinstated fees, sanctions or retaliatory detentions would change the cost and risk of deploying particular tonnage into US and Chinese trades.

storylines.title: Strike threat at LA-Long Beach
storylines.what: The Los Angeles-Long Beach port complex is bracing for a strike as a deadline nears, with employers warning of severe supply chain disruption if talks fail.
storylines.why_it_matters: A stoppage at the largest US West Coast gateway would disrupt container flows, berth availability and inland logistics, with knock-on congestion for vessels scheduled to call.
storylines.latest: More than 110 US trade associations publicly urged employers and union leaders to reach a deal as the strike deadline approaches.

storylines.why_it_matters: Reinstated fees, sanctions or retaliatory detentions would change the cost and risk of deploying particular tonnage into US and Chinese trades.

storylines.title: Strike threat at LA-Long Beach
storylines.what: The Los Angeles-Long Beach port complex is bracing for a strike as a deadline nears, with employers warning of severe supply chain disruption if talks fail.
storylines.why_it_matters: A stoppage at the largest US West Coast gateway would disrupt container flows, berth availability and inland logistics, with knock-on congestion for vessels scheduled to call.
storylines.latest: More than 110 US trade associations publicly urged employers and union leaders to reach a deal as the strike deadline approaches.
sources: More Than 110 Trade Groups Urge Deal as LA-Long Beach Port Strike Deadline Nears
